Both ids pass in isolation on both trees, so they read as load contention rather than a code regression, but a strict zero-added verdict from these two arms alone is unavailable.

the override is applied only when the resolved lane's stop state is 'declared' (if reason and orchestrator_lane_stop['state'] == 'declared'); a --allow-orchestrator-lane REASON passed against a lane that does not declare the orchestrator role is silently accepted and dropped with no warning and no recorded override. A coordinator who deliberately states a reason against a lane whose resolution later changes (e.g. a budget fallback to a non-declaring backend) loses the record without a signal, which is the 'invisible config change' failure §2 exists to prevent.

item_verdicts.diff: read fef2beb97 against base e85fb9cd8 — six files, 200 insertions, no deletions; reckon/cli.py adds the --allow-orchestrator-lane REASON option and threads orchestrator_lane_reason into both plan_dispatch and dispatch; reckon/crew/dispatch.py adds the DispatchPlan.orchestrator_lane_override field, composes it when the stop state is 'declared', flips the stop to state/severity 'overridden' with the reason, and writes the override into the run record; reckon/crew/promotion.py carries record['orchestrator_lane_override'] into the promoted row; reckon/ledger.py adds the field to RECORD_FIELDS and build_record; plus one guard test and one evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node goal (PLAN §2) is that a deliberate dispatch to an orchestrator lane needs a flag whose reason is recorded on the run and reaches the ledger row, the default stops, and the override does not persist across runs. tests/test_the_lane_override_is_explicit_and_recorded.py covers all four: before/after unflagged dispatches record state 'declared' with override None, the flagged dispatch records {'lane':'clive','reason':...}, a launched run carries the field on its live pointer, an empty reason is refused (exit 1, dispatch-refused), and the promoted ledger row carries {'lane':'alpha','reason':...}. Focused gate 10 passed; negative control reddens the ledger assertion EXIT=1 and the restored control passes.
item_verdicts.goal: read the §2 measure and the six-file diff — the flag exists, the reason is recorded on the live run record, it reaches the promoted ledger row, the unflagged default stays a recorded stop per §4, and the reason is scoped to one dispatch by test. The goal is met.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete (repaired from as-delivered blocked at 2026-10-04T23:49:04Z with the as-delivered copy kept at manifest.md.asdelivered); baseline_suite and after_suite are JSON blocks with completed:true, revisions e85fb9cd8 and d90627fb, literal commands and named logs; negative_control_log is a bare path.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the run declared seven paths including reckon/cli.py (not the sibling §3 run's nonexistent reckon/crew/cli.py); the diff writes exactly the six named in changed_paths, all within the declaration, and the worktree is clean at head.

justifications.durability: the behaviour is guarded by tests/test_the_lane_override_is_explicit_and_recorded.py:33-46 (field present and None when unflagged, override dict when flagged), :47-56 (before/after unflagged dispatch proves non-persistence), :97-102 (live-pointer field on a launched run) and :115-126 (promoted row and ledger.runs). The recorded negative control (negative-control.log) mutates the run record to drop the reason and reddens the ledger assertion EXIT=1 (assert None == {'lane':'alpha','reason':'restore a blocked review'}), while restored-control.log passes the unmutated assertion — so the guard is not blind. The field rides ledger.RECORD_FIELDS, so every future row carries it rather than only rows built through the one path.
justifications.evidence: the defect reproduces at base and the fix is shown to work: defect-reproduction.log reddens all three tests at e85fb9cd8 (KeyError 'orchestrator_lane_override', JSONDecodeError on the missing flag, TypeError on the unexpected orchestrator_lane_reason kwarg), and my independent re-run of the same file against the base scratch tree reproduced 3 failed EXIT=1 while the same file at head (fef2beb97) passed 3/3. The focused gate (10 passed), the negative control (EXIT=1) and the restored control (EXIT=0) are all recorded. Docked because the focused-head.log first line mislabels its revision as the base commit, and the added-failure delta of 2 is not retired or attributed by the run's own arms — the repair rationale appeals to a coordinator recheck the reviewed logs do not contain.
justifications.fit: the change follows the established override-flag family (--allow-unreconciled-runs, --allow-unreviewed-plan, --no-watch): one CLI option, one DispatchPlan field, one run-record key, one RECORD_FIELDS entry and one build_record parameter, mirroring unreconciled_override exactly rather than inventing a second provenance path. It adds no new module, reuses the existing stop mapping and promotion plumbing, and the empty-reason refusal reuses CrewError, so the layer sits behind the existing dispatch interface.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all four clauses of §2's measure hold — the flag --allow-orchestrator-lane REASON exists (reckon/cli.py:1766), the reason is recorded on the run (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7339 writes orchestrator_lane_override into the run record), it reaches the ledger row (reckon/crew/promotion.py:8441 plus reckon/ledger.py:170 in RECORD_FIELDS), and it does not persist across runs (proved by the before/after unflagged dispatches). The unflagged default remains the §4 recorded stop (state 'declared'), not a silent launch, so the override is the only way through and it carries its reason. Docked one point only because §2's 'the default is refusal' is presently the recorded-stop form that §4 gates, so the refusal wording is not yet the live behaviour — correct per §4, but the section's own sentence is not literally satisfied.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff writes exactly the six paths in the manifest's changed_paths and all fall within the run's declared seven-path fence (including the correct reckon/cli.py, unlike the sibling §3 run); no figure was written though one was permitted; the worktree is clean at head; the three commits carry conventional subjects with explanatory bodies, no AI trailer, and no plan, sprint or ticket identifiers in messages, symbols, filenames or comments.
